system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
Ryan is packing books into a rectangular box.

All the books are the same size.

[Image: A book and a box. The book measures 20 centimeters by 15 centimeters by 6 centimeters. The box has a length of 36 centimeters, width of 30 centimeters, and height of 20 centimeters.]

What is the largest number of books that will fit inside the box?

Answer: ____

Figure, described in words:
Two 3-dimensional diagrams:
1. A closed rectangular book labeled "Book" with dimensions indicated by double-headed arrows: height/thickness 6 cm, length 20 cm along the left edge, and width 15 cm along the right-front edge.
2. An open rectangular box labeled "Box" with dimensions indicated by double-headed arrows: width 30 cm along the front-left top edge, length 36 cm along the back-right top edge, and vertical height/depth of 20 cm along the inside back corner from top to bottom.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: 12. Stand each book on its 6 cm by 15 cm face so its 20 cm side is vertical, matching the box's 20 cm height. The base is 36 cm by 30 cm. Place 6 cm along the 36 cm length (6 books, exactly 36 cm) and 15 cm along the 30 cm width (2 books, exactly 30 cm), giving 2 × 6 = 12 books in one layer. The box volume is 36 × 30 × 20 = 21,600 cm³ and each book is 20 × 15 × 6 = 1,800 cm³, so 21,600 ÷ 1,800 = 12, which means no more than 12 books can fit.
